question: to the Commission Majdouline Sbai (Verts/ALE), Mounir Satouri (Verts/ALE), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), David Cormand (Verts/ALE), Saskia Bricmont (Verts/ALE), Mélissa Camara (Verts/ALE), Benedetta Scuderi (Verts/ALE), Martin Häusling (Verts/ALE), Jutta Paulus (Verts/ALE), Cristina Guarda (Verts/ALE), Erik Marquardt (Verts/ALE), Rasmus Nordqvist (Verts/ALE), Anna Cavazzini (Verts/ALE), Lena Schilling (Verts/ALE), Thomas Waitz (Verts/ALE), Villy Søvndal (Verts/ALE), Ville Niinistö (Verts/ALE), Martin Hojsík (Renew), Anja Hazekamp (The Left), Martin Günther (The Left), Manon Aubry (The Left), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Maria Noichl (S&D), Estrella Galán (The Left), Emma Fourreau (The Left), Christophe Clergeau (S&D), Leila Chaibi (The Left), Elisabeth Grossmann (S&D), Eric Sargiacomo (S&D), Thomas PellerinCarlin (S&D), Udo Bullmann (S&D), Chloé Ridel (S&D), Bruno Tobback (S&D), Reinier Van Lanschot (Verts/ALE), Anna Strolenberg (Verts/ALE), Kai Tegethoff (Verts/ALE) Subject:

In its chemicals strategy for sustainability published in 20201, the Commission committed to ‘lead by example’ and ‘ensure that hazardous chemicals banned in the European Union are not produced for export’. Yet no legislative proposal has followed, despite an impact assessment that has reportedly been completed but not made public. Meanwhile, exports of pesticides banned for use in the EU continue to rise. In 2024, the EU exported around 122 000 tonnes of such pesticides, 50 % more than in 2018. UN Special Rapporteurs have criticised this double standard for exposing vulnerable populations to hazardous chemicals and undermining the right to a clean and healthy environment. Furthermore, these exports create a ‘boomerang effect’, as residues of banned pesticides can return to the EU through imported food. 1.
Will the Commission finally honour its commitment to ‘lead by example’ and present legislation to prohibit the production and export of pesticides banned in the EU? If not, why not?
Given the significant commercial interests involved, what measures is the Commission taking to prevent undue corporate influence and safeguard public trust in its decisionmaking on this issue?
Will the Commission publish without delay the full impact assessment and related studies, which are financed with public funds?
Commission communication of 14 October 2020 entitled ‘Chemicals Strategy for Sustainability Towards a Toxic-Free Environment’ (COM(2020)/0667). 1
